title: Get up
body:
A difficult day, full of rushing, exam period, setbacks..
In my haste, trying to manage to carry out all my obligations, within the timeframe allotted to us by law (I wonder how I say this while simultaneously not living in 1970),
with a fast stride, enduring the tyranny of the mask, with headphones and a heavy bag on my back, I cross Filippou street heading toward Aristotelous Square.
My step steadily fast, my gaze fixed straight ahead, my mind constructing the plan for the optimal management of the remaining time, and the headphones there, distracting me from every sound dissonance of the city.

Passing right by an elderly lady sitting on a chair, alone outside one of the many furniture stores on that particular street, I feel a pull.
I stop, take off my headphones, and turn my gaze to the lady who was asking for my help.
"My lad, may God keep you well, help me stand up."

I confess I was taken aback.
A few tenths of a second passed until my mind processed whether it was RIGHT to give my hands to this helpless lady and help her stand on her feet.

1. But doesn't she wear a mask?
2. But I'm a random stranger and she's asking me to touch her?
3. But isn't she afraid that I, the careless youth, might have coronavirus and pass it on to her? She belongs to a vulnerable group..
4. Did she really ask me, or does she have some issue? Why get involved now...

I give her my hands and a little of my strength.
She was in pain as she stood up, but finally she stood. Who knows how long she had been waiting for this moment.

The lady was not afraid of coronavirus.
The lady was not afraid of me, the stranger, the contagious and dangerous youth.
The lady asked for something very simple:
to stand up.

Stand up.

y.f.
